lede: An earlier pass of this archive found a Thomas Sinegar living a mile from Hannah Wakefield and called him “the best lead this archive has”, because he was one of only two Sanigers in Bristol who gave their birthplace as Berkley. Then I decided Hannah was not born in Gloucestershire, and spent three days in Somerset. She was born at Berkeley. He is worth going back to.
who: Thomas Saniger, baptised at Berkeley on 3 JULY 1808, son of JOHN SANIGER — Hannah's brother, if the Bristol man is him.

case: Thomas Saniger was baptised at Berkeley on 3 July 1808. At the 1851 census, taken on 30 March, a man born in July 1808 is FORTY-TWO. The enumerator wrote forty-two.
The birthplace is exact, and it is unusual.
He gives BERKLEY — the same idiosyncratic spelling the family tree uses for Hannah's birthplace, and the parish the 1851 census independently gives her.
St Philip and Jacob is the parish adjoining St Paul, where Hannah lived. A mile apart.
And the name Lydia runs through it.

The tree says Hannah's mother was LYDIA. In 1841 a LYDDYA SINEGAR aged seventy is living in Hannah's house at Drivers Fields. In the same census Thomas Sinegar has a daughter LYDIA aged nine. In 1866 his son James christens a daughter LYDIA. Three generations of a name that is not common, in two households a mile apart.
And he named his children after them.

Thomas and Martha had eleven children. Two sons were called JOHN, both dying as infants — his father's name. A daughter was LYDIA — his mother's name on the tree. A daughter, christened at St Philip and Jacob on 4 February 1849, was HANNAH.
against: The marriage to Martha Golding is on a shared tree with no source attached, so the entry that would name Thomas's father has still not been seen.
Their mother's surname — JONES on that tree — is likewise unsourced.
But the sibling link no longer rests on inference. Both baptisms name John Saniger of Berkeley.
verdict: CONFIRMED, later the same day. Hannah's own baptism has been found at Berkeley — HANNAH SANIGOR, 18 August 1804, father JNO SANIGOR — and Thomas was baptised in the same parish to the same father on 3 July 1808. They are brother and sister on the register. What remains unsourced is his marriage: the FamilySearch tree gives MARTHA GOLDING at Bristol St James on 24 August 1828 and attaches no record to it.
